idiom_name: node:diagnostics_channel named channels + process.on('message')/cluster IPC + signal handlers
implementation_notes: Node carries a control channel inside the process: node:diagnostics_channel (stable since v19) creates named channels with publish/subscribe semantics, so a component publishes state and telemetry under a namespaced channel name while a console or exporter subscribes, and hasSubscribers() lets the component skip expensive payload construction when nobody listens. Across processes, cluster/child_process IPC (worker.send / process.on('message')) carries commands to workers, and process signal handlers (process.on('SIGTERM'|'SIGHUP')) provide lifecycle control and configuration reload; the process 'exit' event is the last chance to flush. The classic broker form is only needed when the fleet spans hosts and a broker already exists.
pitfalls: diagnostics_channel subscribers run synchronously inside publish(), so a heavy subscriber slows the publishing code path and a throwing subscriber surfaces as an uncaughtException unless it is guarded.

Channel existence is not delivery: publish() with no subscriber is a silent no-op and cluster IPC drops messages to workers that have already exited, so lifecycle commands still need an acknowledgement.
Replacing the default SIGTERM handler means the process only exits when the handler does: a drain that never resolves leaves a container that ignores its termination signal.

variants.name: Broker control subjects (NATS) with request/reply acknowledgement
variants.implementation_notes: When Node services already talk to a broker, the control bus becomes a subject namespace: components subscribe to control.<component>.cmd, publish heartbeats and status to control.<component>.status, and the console addresses one component or the whole fleet through wildcards (control.*.cmd); request/reply gives the acknowledgement that in-process channels cannot provide across hosts. Use this variant for long-lived services spread over many machines; inside one process or one host the stdlib diagnostics_channel/IPC variant is cheaper and has no infrastructure dependency.
pitfalls: Core NATS is at-most-once: a command published while the component restarts is lost, so destructive operations must use request/reply (or JetStream) and report a timeout instead of assuming success.
Wildcard fan-out (control.*.cmd) reaches every component: maintenance scripts must target explicit subjects for anything destructive.
Status heartbeats are the only liveness signal in this design, so a component that dies without unsubscribing looks alive until the console tracks missed heartbeats.
